description: We’re Caly’s Check Engine Club, a UHRET student team from Öztimurlar MTAL in Bursa, Türkiye. We code in Python, C++, and JavaScript, and somehow convinced Caly to join a NASA hackathon. We’re building an interactive space garage about NASA’s equipment left on the Moon and Mars, with real mission stories and far too many Easter eggs. Looking for people into web development, design, research, or storytelling. Expect actual teamwork and occasional arguments about the font.
summary:
Caly: Left Behind is an interactive educational visual novel that brings the stories of equipment left on the Moon to life.

Players meet Caly, a fictional extraterrestrial explorer who guides them through NASA's Apollo 17 mission. Using authentic NASA photographs, players investigate the Lunar Roving Vehicle, its innovative wheels, the Challenger lunar module's descent stage, and the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP).

Instead of simply reading facts, players discover objects, ask Caly questions, and learn how these machines contributed to lunar exploration and why they remained on the Moon.

The game combines storytelling, interactive exploration, and verified NASA resources to make space history more engaging and accessible. Developed with Ren'Py and available in English and Turkish, it can be played directly in a web browser.

Our goal is to show that equipment left behind can still have a story worth telling.
details:
Our project, Caly: Left Behind, is an interactive visual novel created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We wanted to tell the stories of equipment left behind on the Moon in a way that would be more interesting than simply reading information about them.

The game introduces players to Caly, a fictional extraterrestrial character who acts as their guide. She welcomes the player, introduces the Apollo 17 mission, and explains the history of the equipment that astronauts left behind. Players can interact with different objects, ask Caly questions, and learn why these machines were important to space exploration.

The current version is a playable demo focused on the Apollo 17 mission. It includes the Lunar Roving Vehicle, its wheels, the Challenger lunar module, and the scientific instruments left on the lunar surface. We used real NASA photographs and official NASA resources to make sure the historical and scientific information is accurate.

We developed the game using Ren'Py and Python, with support from OpenAI Codex during development. The game supports both English and Turkish, and we published a browser version using Vercel so anyone can play without downloading anything.

We chose a visual novel format because we wanted players to feel like they were exploring these places with Caly rather than reading a textbook. Our main goal was to make the history of space exploration easier to understand and more enjoyable to discover.

We have completed two versions of Caly: Left Behind. The demo offers a shorter experience focused on exploring Apollo 17 equipment, while the full version includes a longer story, more conversations with Caly, and a more detailed visual novel experience. Both versions are available as separate projects on GitHub.
